newsitem.title: JAPAN: No decision yet on MOF personnel changes - Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: No decision yet on MOF personnel changes - Mitsuzuka.

text.p: No decisions have been made yet on major changes to the Ministry of Finance's personnel, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Friday on his return from China.

Mitsuzuka was speaking after Japanese media reported earlier on Friday that the influential finance official Eisuke Sakakibara, currently director of MOF's International Finance Bureau, was poised to take over as vice finance minister for international affairs.

Asked whether any decisions on personnel changes had been made or if the timing for any changes had been set, Mitsuzuka said: "Personnel changes are not in my mind at all at the moment... I have nothing certain to say at the moment."
Mitsuzuka said he will take up the issue from next week, taking into account personnel changes at other ministries as well.
The Sankei Shimbun said that Sakakibara will be officially appointed vice minister in mid-July, taking over from Takatoshi Kato, who will retire from the post.

If Sakakibara was promoted, it would put him in formal charge of MOF negotiations with other Group of Seven (G7) nations and would be seen as a recognition of his success in turning around the yen's precipitous rise to above 80 yen to the dollar in 1995.
Sakakibara said on Friday in Shanghai before he and Mitsuzuka returned to Tokyo that he did not know anything about the appointment.
